::: {#exr-prac-mle-se}
#### Standard error of an MLE (adapted from @dobson4e, Chapter 5)

Let $\dsn{X} \siid \Pois(\rate)$.

**(a)** Derive the Hessian $\hess(\rate; \vx) = \deriv[2]{\rate}\llik(\rate;\vx)$.

**(b)** Derive the observed information $\oinf(\rate; \vx) = -\hess(\rate; \vx)$.

**(c)** Evaluate $\oinf(\hat\rate_{ML}; \vx)$.

**(d)** Give an approximate 95% confidence interval for $\rate$
using the asymptotic normal distribution of the MLE.
:::

:::{#sol-prac-mle-se}

**(a)**

From @exr-prac-score-zero, $\score(\rate; \vx) = \frac{n\rvarbar}{\rate} - n$.

$$
\ba
\hess(\rate; \vx)
&= \deriv{\rate}\sb{\frac{n\rvarbar}{\rate} - n}
&& \text{(Poisson score)}
\\
&= \deriv{\rate}\sb{n\rvarbar\rate^{-1} - n}
&& \text{(write $\tfrac{n\rvarbar}{\rate}$ as $n\rvarbar\rate^{-1}$)}
\\
&= \deriv{\rate}\sb{n\rvarbar\rate^{-1}} - \deriv{\rate} n
&& \text{(linearity of differentiation)}
\\
&= \deriv{\rate}\sb{n\rvarbar\rate^{-1}} - 0
&& \text{(derivative of a constant)}
\\
&= \deriv{\rate}\sb{n\rvarbar\rate^{-1}}
&& \text{(drop the zero term)}
\\
&= n\rvarbar\deriv{\rate}\rate^{-1}
&& \text{(constant multiple rule)}
\\
&= n\rvarbar\paren{-\rate^{-2}}
&& \text{(power rule)}
\\
&= -n\rvarbar\rate^{-2}
&& \text{(multiply)}
\\
&= -\frac{n\rvarbar}{\rate^2}
&& \text{(write the negative power as a fraction)}
\ea
$$

**(b)**

$$
\ba
\oinf(\rate; \vx)
&= -\hess(\rate; \vx)
&& \text{(observed information is the negative Hessian)}
\\
&= -\paren{-\frac{n\rvarbar}{\rate^2}}
&& \text{(Hessian from (a))}
\\
&= \frac{n\rvarbar}{\rate^2}
&& \text{(two negatives make a positive)}
\ea
$$

**(c)**

Assuming $\rvarbar > 0$
(i.e., at least one $\rvar_\iobs > 0$),
substituting $\hat\rate_{ML} = \rvarbar$:

$$
\ba
\oinf(\hat\rate_{ML}; \vx)
&= \frac{n\rvarbar}{\rvarbar^2}
&& \text{(observed information at $\rate = \rvarbar$)}
\\
&= \frac{n}{\rvarbar}
&& \text{(cancel one factor of $\rvarbar$)}
\ea
$$

**(d)**

By the asymptotic theory of MLEs:

$$
\hat\rate_{ML}
\;\dot\sim\;
\Normal\!\paren{\rate,\; \inv{\einf(\rate)}}
$$

We estimate this asymptotic variance
using the observed information
evaluated at the MLE.
Since $\oinf(\hat\rate_{ML};\vx)^{-1} = \rvarbar/n$:

$$
\SE{\hat\rate_{ML}} \approx \sqrt{\frac{\rvarbar}{n}}
$$

An approximate 95% CI for $\rate$ is:

$$
\hat\rate_{ML} \pm 1.96 \times \sqrt{\frac{\rvarbar}{n}}
= \rvarbar \pm 1.96\sqrt{\frac{\rvarbar}{n}}
$$

:::
